title: Rapid prototyping toolkit: local dev loop + UX notes
content:
Context and intent:
This is a personal sketch for a small internal toolkit to speed up developer iteration when building features that touch inference. The problem: engineering teams spend too much time toggling between local mocks, expensive hosted runs, and flaky env parity (KV cache, batching, tokenization differences). I want a low-friction way to spin up ephemeral sandboxes that mirror Redwood's runtime behaviour enough to validate UX, cost heuristics, and prompt regressions without provisioning Dedicated resources.

Goals (high level):
- Make it trivial to run quick end-to-end experiments locally (CLI + lightweight UI) that approximate hosted behaviour: streaming, partial-prefix caching, quantized model variants, and token cost estimates.
- Capture a reproducible artifact for each experiment (prompt, model config, input sequence, runtime flags, perf/latency/cost results).
- Provide rails for designers/product to validate micro-UX changes (truncation UX, streaming spinners, progressive fidelity fallbacks) with minimal infra overhead.
- Ensure privacy: default to synthetic or redacted data, plus easy redaction tooling for captured artifacts.

Core components (mini PRD):
1) CLI: rp-proto serve / run / record
   - run: takes local file or inline prompt, selects model shim (tiny local quantized model or remote hosted dev token), prints streaming tokens to stdout with metadata.
   - serve: launches a small web UI tied to a run ID for interactive exploration.
   - record: saves prompt, effective token count, model args, timing trace, and a small sanitized transcript JSON artifact.
   Acceptance: a team member can run a 1-turn prompt and produce an artifact in < 20s on laptop.

2) Local runtime shim modes (toggleable):
   - fast-sim: deterministic response sanitizer using cached golden completions (near-zero cost) for UI flows.
   - mini-model: run a small quantized model (ggml/llama2-7b-q4f) for realistic token timings and variation.
   - remote-proxy: route to hosted API with dev token and sampling/cost instrumentation.
   UX need: one flag to switch between modes, and clear cost/latency estimation overlay.

3) Artifact format: "proto-run" (flat fields only)
   - required fields: run_id, created_by, mode, model, prompt_hash, token_estimate, duration_ms, sanitized_transcript, screenshot_paths (optional), tags
   - stored as a single newline-delimited JSON file per run.

4) Quick UI (local web):
   - left: prompt editor with history and templating snippets; right: live streaming output with token-by-token latency bars; footer: cost estimate slider (simulate batch sizes / caching) and export/record button.
   - small viewport for mobile previews to validate truncation/fidelity UX.

User stories (examples):
- As a frontend engineer I want to validate streaming UI under slow-token conditions so I can tune spinner thresholds and skeletons. (Acceptance: capture a run that reproduces the perceived jitter and annotate decision points.)
- As a product manager I want to compare quality delta between default hosted model and a quantized cheaper variant for a set of 25 prompts so I can decide fallback policy. (Acceptance: a downloadable CSV with per-prompt BLEU/embedding-similarity and cost delta.)
- As an SRE I want to simulate micro-burst traffic to observe batching behaviour on a local proxy so we can finalize autoscaling knobs. (Acceptance: synthetic concurrent runs produce aggregated batch histograms.)

Edge cases and constraints:
- Model parity: we will never perfectly match production kernels. Make parity explicit: expose a "parity score" card describing what the mode approximates (timing fidelity, sampling randomness, kv-cache behaviour).
- Data safety: default experiments use synthetic placeholder data. When redaction is disabled, require a one-off consent and record an audit tag.
- Performance: avoid shipping heavy models; prefer orchestration to remote dev accounts for expensive runs.

Open questions / next steps:
- Which tiny model family is easiest cross-platform (M1/Intel/ARM)? ggml- or onnx-backed? (ask infra and release-engineering)
- Format stability: should proto-run be a Redwood-wide tiny spec? Propose PR to infra/observability.
- How to wire this into Console as a "Run locally" button that populates a new artifact into user's drafts? Feels high-value for designers.

Low-fi mock interactions (notes):
- CLI sample:
  rp-proto run --mode mini-model --prompt-file quick-case.txt --record --tags "ux-demo,truncate-test"
  -> prints run-id and URL: http://localhost:PORT/runs/<id>

- UI sample flows:
  1. Paste prompt, pick mode (fast-sim / mini / remote), toggle "redact PII" (on by default), press Stream.
  2. Watch tokens + latency bar increment; toggle cost slider to simulate increased batching.
  3. Click Record -> artifact saved -> shareable link / upload to confluence PR.

Privacy checklist (must-have before sharing artifacts outside team):
- automatic PII detection using simple regexes (emails, phones, SSNs) and heuristics on named entities; default redaction on.
- manual scrub UI that previews the sanitized transcript with inline edit support.
- audit tag + owner field in artifact.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: teams will over-rely on local parity and ship regressions. Mitigation: add "parity note" warnings on artifacts and require an automated smoke test against hosted pipeline for any rollout that used local-only validation.
- Risk: artifact leakage. Mitigation: encryption-at-rest for recorded artifacts + opt-in sharing.

MVP proposal (two-week spike):
Week 1: implement CLI run + fast-sim mode + artifact writer. Minimal UI (static HTML) to view artifacts.
Week 2: add mini-model integration (ggml small), streaming tokens, basic PII redaction, and example runs for UX team.

Deliverables for spike:
- repo: redwood/rapid-proto (initial README + CLI binary)
- 5 example proto-run artifacts (streaming demo, fallback-policy comparison, truncation edge case)
- short demo video (2–3 min) for UX and Product stakeholders

If this resonates I can carve a short RFC and a tiny repo skeleton. Also happy to pair with Mira/Caleb on a spike week.

Quick TODOs (personal):
- ping release-eng re: ggml build matrix (Windows/Mac/Linux)
- draft proto-run JSON schema and post to confluence (link in linked_artifacts)
- sketch UI wireframe + share with UX on Tues

Notes to self:
- keep artifact format intentionally simple (flat fields only) so search & ingestion are easier
- prioritize developer joy: single command to replicate a shared run

End of notes.
